CVE-2026-71397.title: Unbounded request body accumulation on streaming RPCs causes memory exhaustion in grpc_server
CVE-2026-71397.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory and crash the node via an oversized client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request body.

The streaming read clause of 'Elixir.GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler':info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) never checks the configured max_body_size. Only the unary read path enforces that cap. 'Elixir.GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy':reading_stream/1 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy.ex) appends every received chunk to its buffer until a complete length-prefixed message arrives. A client can declare a very large message and send it across many small HTTP/2 DATA frames, and the server buffers all of it.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.0.6.

CVE-2026-77359.title: Jupyter MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding can hijack the Jupyter backend through management routes
CVE-2026-77359.description: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()

When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains
other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash
like:

Oops: general protection fault
KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access
RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503)
Call Trace:
vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419)
do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583)
__x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602)

This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return
value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through
udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being
treated as a folio pointer with obvious results.

Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either
0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

CVE-2026-99364.title: NFSD: Fix out-of-bounds read in the rpc_status dump
CVE-2026-99364.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Fix out-of-bounds read in the rpc_status dump

nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit() loads args->opcnt and
args->ops separately, then walks ops[] before rechecking
rq_status_counter. A COMPOUND that completes between the two loads
runs nfsd4_release_compoundargs(), which zeroes opcnt and points ops
back at the eight-entry inline array. A dump that already sampled an
opcnt of 200 clamps it to the sixteen slots in rq_opnum, then indexes
iops[0..15]. iops is the last member of struct nfsd4_compoundargs and
rq_argp is allocated at exactly that size, so the walk runs off the
end of the allocation. The trailing recheck discards the sampled data,
but the read has already happened. NFSD_CMD_RPC_STATUS_GET carries
no GENL_ADMIN_PERM, so an unprivileged local user can repeat the dump
against a busy server until it lands in the window.

Sample opcnt and ops into locals, then finish the counter recheck
before dereferencing ops.…
